title: Sharp spectral-deficit stability for triangle-free graphs
statement: For every finite simple triangle-free graph $G$, put $m=e(G)$ and let $\lambda(G)$ denote its adjacency spectral radius (with $\lambda(G)=0$ when $G$ has no vertices). Define $D(G)=\min_{A,B\subseteq V(G),\ A\cap B=\varnothing}|E(G)\mathbin{\triangle}E(K_{A,B})|$, where $K_{A,B}$ has all edges between $A$ and $B$ and no other edges on $V(G)$; empty parts are permitted. Then $D(G)\le 3\bigl(m-\lambda(G)^2\bigr)$.
resolution_criteria: A proof must establish the stated inequality for every finite simple triangle-free graph, allowing disconnected graphs and isolated vertices and counting both edge additions and deletions in $D(G)$. A disproof must give a finite simple triangle-free graph and rigorously certify $D(G)>3(e(G)-\lambda(G)^2)$. Numerical eigenvalues or an upper bound on $D(G)$ alone do not certify a counterexample.
neighbours: The same inequality $D(G)\le3(e(G)-\lambda(G)^2)$ restricted to finite simple bipartite graphs.
The same inequality $D(G)\le3(e(G)-\lambda(G)^2)$ restricted to finite simple regular triangle-free graphs.
There exists an absolute constant $C<\infty$ such that $D(G)\le C(e(G)-\lambda(G)^2)$ for every finite simple triangle-free graph $G$.
Every finite simple triangle-free graph $G$ can be made bipartite by deleting at most $e(G)-\lambda(G)^2$ edges.
